key_insight: TEM-invisible vacancy platelets are generally stronger dislocation obstacles than same-size interstitial clusters in Fe–Cr alloys and survive passage, while most interstitial clusters are absorbed.
engineering_relevance: Defect-specific strengths and survival behavior can improve low-dose irradiation-hardening models that otherwise attribute invisible-defect contributions to TEM-visible loops.
method: Molecular dynamics of edge-dislocation interactions at 300 K.
Relaxed 1–3 nm vacancy and mixed Fe–Cr interstitial clusters in Fe–3Cr, Fe–5Cr and Fe–10Cr.
Evaluated obstacle strength, interaction mechanisms and defect survival.
evidence_signal: Vacancy-platelet strength reached about 350 MPa at 2.9 nm independently of Cr content, whereas interstitial-cluster strength varied up to fivefold with local Cr arrangement.
watch_item: Computed barrier strengths (α ≈ 0.02–0.25) are upper bounds from simulations at 300 K, not directly validated macroscopic hardening predictions.
paper_title: Edge-dislocation interactions with sub 3 nm vacancy and interstitial clusters in FeCr alloys: Mechanisms, Obstacle strength and Fate
